messages.subject: Dose-response model centred at zero
parts:
Hi all, 

For dose-response model, the sigm has three unknown hyper parameters as below

y = 1 + f(x, "sigm") <=> y = alpha + beta * x / (1 + (L50/x)^n )

I want the response curve to be zero at L50 and thus supports both negative and positive values. This can be achieved with fixing beta=1, and subtract the response curve with a half; then new alpha* will absorb the beta. However, I don't know how to specify the subtraction. Is it correct to do:

v=rep(-.5, number of experiments) 

and put 

y = 1 + f(x, "sigm", hyper=list(theta1=list(initial=1, fixed=TRUE))) + offset(v) 

in the model. 

I do not want this term to be absorbed in the intercept.

Thanks

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Dose-response model centred at zero
parts:
if you do

y ~ 1 + ....

or

y ~ 1 + offset(v)

then the intercept will just adapt by subtracting approximately the
mean of v.

if the v = rep(v0, n), ie, the same, then it will be exact cancellation
with a (default) uniform prior for the intercept.

if you need to curve to pass through a spesific point, would it be
helpful to force it trough a datapoint with high precision?

H

Thanks Håvard, so may be offset is not what I wanted as the sigm term does not 
know it should be offset against v.

Regarding forcing the curve to pass through a specific point (here when x=LD50, 
sigm=beta/2), I think I cannot do that because both beta & L50 are parameters?
That's why I tried to force beta=1 and subtract .5.

I imagine something like: 

x2=x
z = rep(-.5, n)
y ~ 1 + f(x, "sigm", ...) + f(x2, z, model="iid", hyper=list(theta=list(initial=12, fixed=TRUE)))

but x2 mean would be 0 not 1...

Thanks,
